title: Tryb przypuszczający · liczba mnoga
note: B1 Block 4 closer, James's locked decision #3: PLURAL conditional, deferred until after the virile block because it rides -li/-ły. No new formation rule: by attaches to the plural L-form exactly as it attached to the singular one in b1_conditional_sg, and the person markers are the ones already owned from byliśmy/byłyście/byliście/byłyście (a2_past_plural) — my takes -śmy, wy takes -ście, oni/one take nothing extra, mirroring on/ona taking nothing extra in the singular unit. The virile/non-virile choice on my/wy/oni/one is not new either — it is the same 'at least one man?' test from b1_virile_past, now asked of the conditional instead of the plain past. Verbs: chcieć (full 6-slot paradigm: my/wy/oni-one x virile/non-virile, the politeness payoff), kupić (my + oni/one, 4 forms), zrobić (wy + oni/one, 4 forms) — 14 teaches_lemmas total, same load as the singular unit. One flagged irregularity: chcieć's virile plural stem is chcie- (chcieli) while its non-virile/singular stem is chcia- (chciały, chciał, chciała) — a genuine vowel alternation, not a typo. This is NOT explained as a rule here, same conservative choice b1_conditional_sg already made for chciał/chciała itself (catalogue: 'e→a shift deliberately unexplained until B1'); chcieli/chciały are handed over as memorized whole forms, exactly like chciał/chciała were. kupić and zrobić carry no such alternation (kupi-/zrobi- stem throughout), so most of the unit is the clean regular case. Subjects for the oni/one forms use real virile/non-virile nouns already owned from the virile block and b1_people (studenci, pracownicy, nauczyciele, kobiety, turystki) rather than bare pronouns, so the 'which group?' test has real content to bite on. Both-gender-equivalent (virile/non-virile) production, as everywhere in this block. teaches_lemmas also lists the six bare plural-past stems (chcieli/chciały, kupili/kupiły, zrobili/zrobiły) with no by attached — the intro tables show them as the literal stepping stone to the -by- forms and quiz uses them as discrimination distractors (plain past vs conditional), so they are genuinely first-taught here, same treatment b1_virile_past gave pracowali/pracowały.

intro.title: We, you all, they would: the plural echo
intro.body:
You already build he-would and she-would by adding -by to the past form: chciał + by = chciałby. Plural does the exact same thing to the plural past forms you already own from oni/one.

1. Take the plural past — chcieli (a group with a man), chciały (a group of women).
2. Add -by — chcieliby, chciałyby. That is already they-would.
3. For we and you-all, add the same endings you know from byliśmy/byłyście, after the by — chcielibyśmy, chciałybyście.

Nothing new is happening except which pronoun is speaking. The choice between -li- and -ły- is the same test as always: at least one man in the group?
intro.body_pl: Forma przeszła (mnoga) + by + końcówka z byliśmy: chcieli + by + śmy = chcielibyśmy.

intro.title: Same test as byli/były
intro.body: You met this exact split already — it decided byli vs były, and studenci pracowali vs kobiety pracowały. The conditional does not add a new question. It just asks the same one about a would.
intro.body_pl: Studenci pracowali. Kobiety pracowały. Studenci chcieliby kawę. Kobiety chciałyby herbatę.

examples.en: We were at work. → We would like coffee. (a group with a man)
We were at home. → We would like tea. (a group of women)

intro.title: Same glue on kupić and zrobić
intro.body: kupić and zrobić do not have chcieć's spelling quirk — their plural past is one stem all the way through, so the pattern is completely regular.
intro.body_pl: kupili + by + śmy = kupilibyśmy. zrobili + by + ście = zrobilibyście.

rows: you all would make (with a man)

intro.title: Real groups, real would
intro.body: The learner already met these nouns as virile or non-virile subjects for plain past. The same choice now feeds the conditional: studenci is a group that can include a man, so it always takes the -li- forms; kobiety and turystki never do, so they always take -ły-.
intro.body_pl: Studenci chcieliby kawę. Kobiety chciałyby herbatę. Pracownicy kupiliby prezent.

match.en: you all would like (with a man)
you all would make (with a man)

quiz.prompt: We would like (a group with a man) →
quiz.explain: chcieli + by + śmy — the same -śmy you know from byliśmy, on the virile plural stem.

quiz.prompt: We would like (a group of women) →
quiz.explain: chciały + by + śmy, like byłyśmy — the -ł- stem, not -li-.
studenci can include a man, so oni chcieliby — chcieli + by, no ending after by for they, same as chciałby took none for he.
kobiety is never virile, so one chciałyby — chciały + by.
kupić has no vowel quirk: kupili + by + śmy, fully regular.
pracownicy is virile: kupili + by, no ending after by for they.
turystki is a group of women: kupiły + by.

quiz.prompt: You all would make (a group with a man) →
quiz.explain: zrobili + by + ście, like byliście — no vowel quirk on zrobić.
kobiety has no men in it, so it needs the -ły- stem: chciały + by, not chcieli + by.

type_items.explain: chcieli + by + śmy. chcieli is chcieć's virile past — a spelling fact to memorize, like chciał/chciała already were.
